LESSON: BOOK HANDLING.

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP1
Subject: General
Strand: READING
Topic 2.1: Book handling.
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Book handling., part of READING in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP1 General.

Key inquiry question: when How do you take care of books?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Book handling. together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication and collaboration: Teamwork as the learner collaboratively takes turns in keeping books in the bookshelf.

Values:
• Responsibility is developed as the learner opens book pages appropriately and learns to care for their own books by

arranging them properly.

• Integrity is developed as the learner learns to always care for books even without the supervision of others.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skill of personal organisation and management as the learner acquires skills of organising own books and keeping them in

good condition.

Link to other Learning Areas: Proper book handling and care is necessary across all other learning areas as they handle their

books daily.

Suggested learning resources: Books, magazines, pictures on a chart showing books arranged properly, book holders.
